title: Unified Inference API PRD: Chat/Completions/Embeddings/Rerank + Launch Readiness Playbook
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a single, unified Inference API surface that consolidates chat, completions, embeddings, and reranking into a coherent developer experience for the hosted product. The goal is to launch an opinionated, backwards-compatible API that enables low-friction migration from existing endpoints and supports robust production characteristics: predictable latency, cost controls, versioning, and observability.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Self-serve onboarding for common use cases (chat, single-turn completion, bulk embeddings, rerank pipelines) with <200ms p50 generation for short messages on verified models.
- Clear migration path from older endpoints with minimal client change (compat shims where needed).
- Launch checklist completed: SDKs, docs, console routing, SLOs, rollout gating, and security review.
- No high-severity production regressions in the first 30 days post-launch.

Scope:
In-scope:
- API surface: /v1/infer/chat, /v1/infer/completions, /v1/infer/embeddings, /v1/infer/rerank. Unified auth and usage metering.
- Streaming support for chat/completions.
- Batch endpoints for embeddings (bulk mode) and rerank (candidate list input).
- Structured output options (format enforcement + schema validation hooks).
- Model pinning and version field in request.
- Default fallback routing policies (model family fallback + graceful degradation).
- Console onboarding flow, token-level cost breakdown, and per-route dashboards.
Out-of-scope for initial launch:
- Dedicated/Dedicated-only features (reserved capacity UI flows).
- On-prem installer packaging.
- Advanced auto-quantization recommendations in Optimize (will be part of later cycle).

Requirements (high-level):
1) API Design and Backwards Compatibility- Single auth token; same rate limit counters as existing hosted API but configurable by billing tier.
- Query parameters: model, version, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stream=true/false, response_schema, deterministic_hint.
- Error semantics compatible with existing OpenAPI-based encoding with addition of clear retryable vs non-retryable codes for fallback routing.

2) Chat/Completions Behavior- Chat supports role-delimited messages with optional function-calling spec.
- System messages allowed and preserved by default; early warning if system messages exceed token budget.
- Streaming must emit deltas consistent with token boundaries, include metadata frames for model_version and kv_cache_hit (when provided by runtime).

3) Embeddings- Bulk embedding endpoint supports up to 4096 inputs per request; response order must match input order.
- Metadata: model name, dimension, latency_ms and cost_estimate fields in meta.
- Provide distance metric param: cosine | dot | l2 for returned vectors (default cosine).

4) Rerank- Accepts list of candidates and query; returns ordered candidate ids with score and optional logit_breakdown.
- Support two operational modes: score-only and score+rescore (returns regenerated short passage if requested).

5) Performance and Operational- Runtime should support prefix/KV caching with transparent hints from client for repeated context.
- Autoscaling policies for hosted capacity to keep P90 latency within target under expected traffic shape.

6) Observability & Rollout- Per-route SLOs, token-level cost metrics, anomaly alerts for quality regressions (integrates with evals harness).

Trade-offs and decisions so far:
- We will not attempt 1:1 API parity with external vendors; we provide a compatibility layer for the most common OpenAI-compatible fields and map the rest to Redwood primitives. This reduces launch complexity.
- Streaming frames will carry minimal metadata to avoid bloating the stream; additional diagnostics available via console trace logs.
- We will enable the structured-output enforcement opt-in instead of opt-out to reduce risk of breaking existing clients.

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied before "In Review" -> "Planned" gating to dev):
AC-1: Spec published and reviewed in RFC with SDK teams and infra -- sign-off from SDK lead and Runtime lead.
AC-2: End-to-end happy path for each surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) covered by integration tests against staging models and passes in nightly CI.
AC-3: SDKs (Node/Python/Go) implement the new endpoints, with examples and migration guide included in docs.
AC-4: Console pages for per-route latency/cost and rollout control exist and linked from PRD.
AC-5: SLOs defined and alerting configured; runbooks created for common incidents (rate limiting, model OOM, fallback faults).
AC-6: Security review passed and KMS integration validated for logs containing sensitive prompt data (masking + retention policy).
AC-7: Load test demonstrates required throughput and keeps error rates below 0.5% at expected peak load for each route.

API Contract Summary (developer-facing snippet):
- POST /v1/infer/chat
  body: {"model": "string", "version": "string", "messages": [{"role":"system|user|assistant","content":"string"}], "max_tokens":int, "stream":bool, "response_schema":object?} -> stream|json response with {choices:[{message, finish_reason}], meta:{model_version, latency_ms}}
- POST /v1/infer/completions
  body: {prompt(s), model, params...} -> streaming json chunking or batched completions array
- POST /v1/infer/embeddings
  body: {inputs:[string], model, metric:"cosine"} -> {data:[{embedding:[], input_index}], meta:{dimension, latency_ms}}
- POST /v1/infer/rerank
  body: {query, candidates:[{id, text}], mode:"score|rescore"} -> {ranked:[{id,score,explanation?}], meta:{latency_ms}}

Rollout and Launch Plan:
- Canary rollout (Week 0): 5% traffic to unified API via routing rules; smoke tests and integration checks run every 5 minutes.
- Gradual ramp (Week 1): 5% -> 25% -> 50%, each step gated by success criteria (P50/P90 latency, error rates, and quality evals on sampled prompts).
- Full switch (Week 2): remaining traffic migrated with immediate fallback rules to previous endpoints for >2x latency or >1% error rate.
- Post-launch monitoring (30 days): daily quality checks vs baseline eval set; automated alerts on quality regressions.

Launch Checklist (owner initials in parentheses):
- API spec finalized and published (EP)
- SDKs released with migration guide (OC)
- Console routes & dashboards created and linked (PM)
- Billing mapping and quota config validated (Finance/BI)
- E2E tests and load tests passing in staging (ENG)
- Security review + KMS verification complete (Sec)
- Runbooks and on-call rotations updated (SRE)
- Docs: quickstarts, migration guide, changelog (DX)
- Advertising/announce plan and support playbook (GTM)

Dependencies:
- Runtime: prefix/KV cache telemetry extension (ENG-3777)
- SDK: streaming protocol support for Go (SDK-219)
- Observability: tokenized cost pipeline instrumentation (OBS-112)

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Regression in output quality when using fallback model variants. Mitigation: automated evals against critical prompt set and pessimistic fallback ordering; roll back quickly if regression > 5% in precision metrics.
- Risk: Increased cost from unbounded embeddings bulk jobs. Mitigation: per-request quotas, rate limiting, and warning headers for heavy jobs.
- Risk: Streaming edge cases across proxies. Mitigation: add non-streamed fallback path and streaming health checks in the console.

Open Questions (to resolve before full rollout):
- Should the reranker accept raw HTML in candidate texts or do we require sanitized plain text?
- What is the deprecation window for legacy endpoints after full switch? Proposed: 90 days with migration metrics.
